title: Walk-charge maximizers are semi-convergent near-returns of log2(3/2)
statement: Every maximizer of the coupled exponent-walk charge over nonnegative closed walks with a prescribed (o, e) is a concatenation of primitive near-returns to the band [0, 1) whose type vectors (a, r) are semi-convergents of alpha = log2(3/2). At leftover (L, o_min(L)) the maximizer is the ceiling Christoffel word of slope o/L.
mathematical_domain: Juggler cycle finance / exponent-walk optimal control
tested_range: all feasible (L, o) with L <= 24; leftover maximizers at L = 19, 84, 1054; B/L table from the committed 19-row walk-charge survey at floor 26254995
notes: Phase 0 is computationally verified: 123/123 small maximizers and the three leftover itineraries split into types (2,1) and (1,1) only, and the leftover itineraries equal the Christoffel words already in cycle_christoffel. This is a statement about the u >= 0 charge relaxation, not about realized cycle itineraries. The one-parameter leftover-cell slogan stays refuted (juggler_christoffel_one_parameter). The dream uniform ratio B/theta < 1 at a fixed floor is false (survey row L=176251, margin 0.159) and is the same shape as juggler_baker_kills_near_convergents. Not a halt theorem.
